subject: Vocabulary
topic: Word Roots — PORT (carry/bring): import, export, transport, deportation, portfolio
description: Latin root PORT (portare = to carry): import, export, transport, deport, support, portfolio, portly, portage, report — meaning, usage, cloze, fill-in-blank, antonym/synonym.

questions.stem: The word 'TRANSPORT' contains the Latin root PORT. What does PORT mean in this context?

options.option_text: Carry — TRANS (across) + PORT (carry) = carry across
Move — 'move' is the effect, not the root meaning of PORT itself
Place — PORT does not mean 'place'; that would be LOC or SITUS
Send — 'send' is the meaning of MIT/MISS, not PORT

questions.explanation: ROOT: PORT/PORTARE (Latin) = to CARRY or BRING. TRANS + PORT = carry across. PORT FAMILY: import (carry in), export (carry out), transport (carry across), deport (carry away, expel), support (carry from below), report (carry back), portable (can be carried), comport (carry oneself = behave), portfolio (porta + foglio = carry + sheet = folder of documents). EXAM APPLICATION: knowing PORT unlocks the meaning of unfamiliar derivatives like 'importune' (to burden/carry repeatedly = to pester) or 'portage' (carrying boats overland).

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The government decided to ______ the foreign national for violating visa conditions.

options.option_text: deport — DE (away) + PORT (carry) = carry away; legally expel from a country
export — EXPORT applies to goods, not to people under immigration law
transport — transport means moving from place to place, not a legal expulsion order
import — IMPORT means bringing in, the opposite direction of the required action

questions.explanation: DEPORT: DE (away, down, from) + PORT (carry) = formally remove a foreign national from a country. Legal/official connotation. DEPORTATION: the noun form, frequently used in news and banking GK. CONTRAST: 'extradite' = surrender a person to a foreign state (for criminal prosecution); 'deport' = expel for immigration violations. DEPORTATION vs EXILE: deportation = government removes non-citizen; exile = citizen banished from their own country. USAGE: 'The illegal immigrant was deported back to his home country.'

questions.stem: The word 'PORTFOLIO' comes from PORT + FOGLIO (Latin/Italian for 'sheet/leaf'). Which of the following best captures the extended meaning of 'portfolio' in finance?

options.option_text: A collection of investments held by an individual or institution — the 'folder of documents' extended to a collection of assets
A single high-value bond issued by a government — too narrow; portfolio implies a collection, not one item
The official record of a company's liabilities — that is a balance sheet, not a portfolio (not this)
A regulatory filing submitted to SEBI — that is a prospectus or disclosure form, not a portfolio (not this)

questions.explanation: PORTFOLIO: originally 'case for carrying papers' (porta + foglio). Extended meanings: (1) FINANCE: all investments (stocks, bonds, funds) held by an investor. (2) POLITICS: the responsibilities assigned to a minister ('minister without portfolio' = no specific department). (3) ART: a collection of an artist's work samples. PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT: diversified portfolio reduces risk (don't put all eggs in one basket). SEBI REGISTERED PORTFOLIO MANAGER: licensed to manage client portfolios in India. PYQ BANKING GK: portfolio investment, FPI (Foreign Portfolio Investment) vs FDI (Foreign Direct Investment).

questions.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The surgeon's calm manner helped him ______ himself with great dignity throughout the difficult procedure.

options.option_text: comport — COMPORT (COM+PORT) = carry oneself, behave in a particular manner
import — import means to bring goods or ideas in, not to conduct oneself
support — support means to bear weight or back up; doesn't mean to conduct oneself
transport — transport means to carry across a distance, not to conduct or present oneself

questions.explanation: COMPORT: COM (together/with) + PORT (carry) = to carry oneself = to behave/conduct oneself. 'Comport oneself' is always reflexive. USAGE: formal or literary. 'He comported himself with grace.' DEPORTMENT: another PORT derivative = bearing, manner of walking/behaving. 'Her deportment was impeccable.' COMPORT vs DEPORT: comport = carry oneself (behaviour); deport = carry away (immigration). Both share PORT = carry but prefix changes direction. PYQ VOCAB: comport, deportment — occasionally appear in RC passages or vocabulary matching.

questions.stem: The word 'IMPORTUNE' shares the PORT root. Which of the following best describes its meaning?

options.option_text: To trouble or pester persistently with requests — originally 'to bring burden upon repeatedly'
To import goods from a foreign nation — confuses with 'import' due to similar spelling
To cause great misfortune or disaster — incorrect; that would be 'unfortunate' or 'calamitous'
To announce or report an important finding — incorrect; that is closer to 'report' or 'publish'

questions.explanation: IMPORTUNE: IM + PORTUNE (related to PORT — carry, burden). To pester, to make persistent and intrusive requests. 'The vendor importuned the tourists all day.' IMPORTUNATE (adj): troublesomely persistent. IMPORTUNITY (noun): persistent troubling demands. EXAM USE: importune appears in RC passages describing aggressive salespeople, beggars, or petitioners. DON'T CONFUSE: importune ≠ import + fortune. The -une suffix connects to 'opportune' (at the right time) — importunate = NOT at the right time, hence 'inopportune and persistent'. PYQ: high-difficulty vocabulary in IBPS PO/SBI PO RC passages.

questions.stem: Which pair of words BOTH contain the PORT root with the core meaning 'carry'?

options.option_text: Portage and rapport — 'portage' carries boats overland; 'rapport' shares re+apport (French PORT family)
Portable and deportment — both derive from PORT (carry): portable = can be carried; deportment = manner of carrying oneself
Portal and portfolio — 'portal' comes from PORTA (gate/door), not from PORTARE (carry) (not this)
Portion and transport — 'portion' comes from PORTIO (share/division), unrelated to PORTARE (not this)

questions.explanation: PORTABLE: PORT (carry) + ABLE = capable of being carried. DEPORTMENT: DE + PORT + MENT = the manner in which one carries oneself (bearing, posture, behaviour). PORTAL: from PORTA = gate/door (not portare = carry) — portal, port (harbour), portico. These look like PORT words but come from a different Latin root. PORTION: from PORTIO = share, allotment (not portare) — portion, proportion, apportion. The distinction between PORTA (gate), PORTIO (share), and PORTARE (carry) is a vocabulary-enrichment trap frequently used in IBPS PO reading comprehension.

questions.stem: The government's ______ strategy shifted manufacturing supply chains back home from overseas factories, reducing the country's dependence on foreign imports.

options.option_text: import-substitution — replacing imports with domestically produced goods
export-promotion — this increases exports; it does not reduce import dependence directly
deportation — deportation applies to persons, not to industrial or trade policy
transport-diversification — refers to logistics modes; not a trade policy for supply chains

questions.explanation: IMPORT SUBSTITUTION INDUSTRIALISATION (ISI): economic policy to reduce dependence on foreign imports by developing domestic industries that produce those goods locally. INDIA CONTEXT: ISI was the dominant policy 1950s–1980s under Nehru and Indira Gandhi — heavy industries, steel, machines were produced domestically under protection. CURRENT PARALLEL: 'Make in India' and 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' (Self-Reliant India) are modern variants of ISI strategy. CONTRAST: Export-led growth (South Korea, Taiwan) focuses on boosting exports for foreign exchange, not reducing imports. PYQ BANKING/ECONOMICS: ISI vs export-promotion debate in Indian economic history.
